title: Listening Comprehension
intro: Listen to a classroom dialogue, then answer multiple choice questions. You can replay the dialogue as many times as you want.

lines.speaker: Ms. Rivera
lines.text: Today each group will choose one traditional tale and explain the lesson it teaches.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Can our group choose a trickster story? I like stories where a small character outsmarts a big one.

lines.speaker: Ms. Rivera
lines.text: Yes, but remember to explain whether the trick is helpful or harmful.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: We should also include one proverb that matches the story, like honesty is the best policy.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Good idea. I will write about the characters, and you can find the proverb.

lines.speaker: Ms. Rivera
lines.text: Excellent. Be ready to share your central idea tomorrow.

questions.q: Why does Mia like trickster stories?
choices: A small character may outsmart a big one.

questions.q: What does Ms. Rivera want students to explain about the trick?
choices: Whether it is helpful or harmful

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: I mixed up theme and central idea again.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: Our anchor chart says theme is the lesson of a story. Central idea is the most important point of a text.

lines.speaker: Noah
lines.text: So if a story shows that greed causes trouble, that is the theme?

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: Right. And if an article explains that legends often teach cultural values, that is a central idea.

lines.speaker: Ava
lines.text: Look at what they say, do, think, and learn. Those details help you describe them.

questions.q: What two skills does Noah mix up?
According to Ava, what is theme?
Which example does Noah give for theme?
What details help readers describe characters?
choices: What they say, do, think, and learn

questions.q: What is Ava doing in this dialogue?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Our presentation is on a legend about too much heat from the sky.

lines.speaker: Lily
lines.text: Then we should explain the setting first. It happens long ago, before people understood the sun in a scientific way.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I can draw a picture with a caption. The caption will explain why the land is drying up.

lines.speaker: Lily
lines.text: I will talk about the main problem. The characters do not use their power wisely.

lines.speaker: Lily
lines.text: Maybe power should be used carefully. That matches the story and the picture.

choices: A legend about too much heat from the sky

questions.q: What literary element does Lily want to explain first?
What is the main problem Lily mentions?
choices: The characters do not use their power wisely.
